newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Cancer scare hits Philippine bread sales.
newsitem.headline: Cancer scare hits Philippine bread sales.

text.p: Philippine bread sales have fallen 20 percent over the last two months because of fears that a chemical used in the country's favourite breakfast roll may cause cancer, a leading flour miller said on Friday.
"Bread sales dropped by 20 percent in the past two months due to a cancer scare on pan de sal," Philippine Association of Flour Millers Inc (PAFMIL) executive director Ric Pinca told Reuters.
Pan de sal are small bread rolls commonly eaten for breakfast.
Pinca said fears that potassium bromate, used by bakers to give pan de sal a fluffy texture, might cause cancer had depressed local bread sales.
Health authorities have given local flour millers and bakers until the end of the month to find an alternative to potassium bromate.
PAFMIL and local bakers said they had not found a suitable alternative and that there were no studies to show the use of potassium bromate in small quantities caused cancer in humans.
